text:
maria (Support): Heads-up — we have an urgent escalation from 3 customers in EMEA: sudden spikes in request latency (1s -> 700ms -> 2.5s) and some 502s. They say calls are routed to us-east despite >X-Region header set to eu-west. Billing reports token spikes due to repeated retries. Can SRE look?

eric (SRE): ack. Any recent deploys or config changes to routing/healthchecks?

maria (Support): No customer-side changes. They say it started ~10:23 UTC. I attached a minimal repro: curl to our API endpoint from an EU host shows long TTFB and sometimes immediate 502. Logs included below.

maria (Support): ```
# from customer EU VM
curl -i -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# sometimes returns 200 after 1.2s
# sometimes returns 502 immediately
# tcpdump shows SYN/ACK to 52.14.xx.xx (us-east LB) not eu-west IP
```

healthcheck-bot: alert: region-healthcheck-eu-west flapping (3 failures in last 2m) :rotating_light:

eric (SRE): Interesting — healthcheck flapping could trigger our smart routing fallback to us-east. Can you share the healthcheck probe config for eu-west and the LB mapping?

kyle (Platform): copying config: probe path=/heartbeat, method=GET, timeout=1s, interval=10s, failure_threshold=3, success_threshold=2. LB routes based on active-health and control-plane decides global fallback after 2 consecutive region failures.

julia (Reliability): two immediate red flags: timeout=1s is tight for cold starts and network jitter; failure_threshold=3 + global fallback=2 means a region can be marked down quickly. Also /heartbeat goes through app load path that hits a maintenance-only handler on one VM. That VM is returning 503 intermittently during control-plane healthcheck bursts.

eric (SRE): repro steps I'm going to run from an EU probe VM: 1) curl -v -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health 2) tracepath to LB 3) fetch /heartbeat on all backend instances. Will paste results.

eric (SRE): ```
# from eu-probe
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_starttransfer}s\n" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/heartbeat
# output: sometimes 200 0.95s, sometimes 503 0.03s
# dig shows LB A record rotates between eu-west-ip and us-east-ip depending on active-health
# ssh to backend-12 (one host) and curl localhost:8080/heartbeat -> returns 503 with stacktrace indicating admin-only handler
```

maria (Support): Customers reported retries from client side — likely duplicate generations counted in billing. They want immediate mitigation.

julia (Reliability): Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase probe timeout to 3s and failure_threshold to 5 to reduce false positives 2) change probe path to /live (lightweight, served by all app nodes, not admin handler) 3) disable global fallback for tiered enterprise customers for 30m while we stabilize. Which can we do quickly?

kyle (Platform): I can push probe config change to eu-west within 10m (hotpath change). Path change requires a quick LB config update — need 15–20m including smoke tests. Disabling global fallback is a config toggle in control-plane — I can do that for a customer-set in 5m.

eric (SRE): Do we have a runbook update to avoid /heartbeat hitting admin-only instance? If not, we should mark /heartbeat deprecated in proxy and migrate to /live. I'll prepare a small proxy rule to route /heartbeat to all app pools.

maria (Support): I propose we: A) disable global fallback for affected customers now B) increase failure_threshold and timeout in eu-west probe C) change probe path to /live once LB change is done D) follow-up with customer explaining root cause and billing remediation. They asked for credits.

julia (Reliability): +1. Also we should capture timeline for billing team. Suggest job: collect request_ids from sample windows (10:20–10:40 UTC) and compute duplicate generation counts.

kyle (Platform): Actioning now: toggling fallback for the 3 customers (ids C-123, C-456, C-789). ETA 5m. Then I'll patch probe timeout->3s and failure_threshold->5. Will post diff.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: platform-config/eu-health-probe-change -> approved by kyle -> rollout started.

eric (SRE): I pushed a proxy rule to avoid admin-only node for /heartbeat. Please validate: ```
# check across nodes
for n in backend-{10..15}; do ssh $n curl -sS localhost:8080/live || echo "$n failed"; done
```

maria (Support): Customer on call confirms latency improving after ~12m, no more routing to us-east visible in tcpdump. They still want billing credits.

julia (Reliability): Postmortem to include root cause: healthcheck endpoint hitting admin-only instance + aggressive probe thresholds + global fallback policy too eager. Remediation: migrate to /live, raise probe timeouts, add region-specific heartbeat with stronger quorum (require N healthy nodes not LB single-check), add canary check window before global fallback triggers.

eric (SRE): Follow-ups: - kyle: revert probe config if smoke fails (T+30m) - juila: prepare canary policy PR for control-plane fallback logic - maria: collect customer request_ids and billing deltas and open support credit ticket - me: run 48h monitoring job to ensure flapping stops

kyle (Platform): Changes rolled out: timeout=3s, failure_threshold=5, probe path pointed to /live across eu-west pools. Rolling restart avoided. Monitoring shows health stable.

healthcheck-bot: resolved: region-healthcheck-eu-west stable.

maria (Support): Customer accepted provisional credit offer, asked for written RCA. I'll draft and loop you all in. Thanks 🙏

julia (Reliability): We'll schedule a short postmortem doc this week and attach logs + config diffs. Good catch everyone. :white_check_mark:
